title: Next generation engineering of conditional mouse alleles with loxP and FRT sites by dual RMCE.
protocol: Pre-warm the media, Trypsin-EDTA (1x), and D-PBS before use.
Split ES cells every two days under sterile conditions.
Ensure sufficient number of dishes with confluent and mitotically-arrested feeder cells are available when splitting ES cells.
Dissociate ES cells by gentle pipetting to avoid the creation of air bubbles, ensuring a single-cell suspension.
Check the quality of the single-cell suspension under the microscope before proceeding.
Replace the feeder cell medium with medium containing 10 μg/ml Mitomycin C.
Incubate the plates for 2 hours at 37°C in a tissue culture incubator.
Remove the Mitomycin C medium.
Wash the plates three times with D-PBS (with Mg<sup>2+</sup>/Ca<sup>2+</sup>).
Add feeder cell medium and return the plates to the incubator.
Thaw one aliquot of frozen parental ES cells in a waterbath at 37°C.
Transfer the contents into a 15-ml tube containing 10 ml of ES cell medium.
Centrifuge at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of ES cell medium.
Plate onto a 6-cm dish containing 3 ml of ES cell medium.
Check the cells under the microscope on day 2.
Refresh the medium on day 2.
Passage the cells from a 6-cm to a 10-cm dish on day 3.
Wash the plate with 2 ml of Trypsin-EDTA (1x).
Replace with 1.5 ml of Trypsin-EDTA (1x) and return to the incubator for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Tap the plate gently and pipette the ES cells up and down 5-7 times with a 2 ml pipette.
Check the single cell status under a microscope.
Add 4 ml of ES cell medium and pipette 2-3 more times using a 5 ml pipette.
Return the dish to the incubator for 15 minutes.
Transfer the ES cells by gently swirling the dish and collecting the 4.5 ml ES cell medium into a 15-ml tube.
Centrifuge the cells.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 ml of ES cell medium.
Plate the harvested ES cells into one 10-cm dish with mitotically-arrested feeder cells and 8 ml of ES cell medium.
Split the cells into two 10-cm dishes if they have grown to almost 80% confluency.
Monitor the cells for potential confluency and colony morphology.
Refresh the medium.
Split the cells onto four to six 10-cm dishes with feeder cells at a ratio of 1:4 to 1:6.
Resuspend the cells in 7 ml ES cell medium for plating.
Monitor the cells.
Refresh the medium.
Electroporate ES cells using 0.24 kV and 475 μF conditions.
Use approximately 1.5 × 10^7 cells in 0.8 ml D-PBS per cuvette.
Prepare experimental cuvette 1 with ES cells (1.5 × 10^7) + pDIRE (50 μg), + replacement vector (50 μg).
Prepare control cuvette with ES cells (1.5 × 10^7) + pDIRE (50 μg).
Trypsinize ES cells from approximately 70% confluent 10-cm dishes.
Ensure ES cells form a single-cell suspension by pipetting in Trypsin-EDTA solution if necessary.
Prepare gelatin-coated tissue culture dishes by covering the surface with 0.1% gelatin, incubating for 5 minutes at room temperature, and then aspirating the solution.
Allow gelatin-coated plates to dry for 10 minutes.
Collect ES cells after 10 min adherence to remove feeder cells carefully.
Pool ES cell suspensions from various dishes in 50-ml tubes and ensure homogeneity.
Transfer a 100 μl aliquot into a 1.5-ml tube containing 0.9 ml of ES cell medium for a 1/10 dilution.
Count the cells and calculate the total amount of ES cells in each 50 ml-tube.
Centrifuge the ES cells at 1000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in D-PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ at a final concentration of 1.875×10⁷ cells per ml.
Add 0.8ml ES cell suspension to each DNA-containing cuvette using a 1-ml cell culture grade plastic pipette.
Mix the solution by pipetting up and down 2 to 3 times to ensure homogeneous dispersion of the DNA.
Pulse each of the cuvettes and place them on ice immediately after electroporation.
Let the cuvettes rest on ice for 20 minutes following electroporation.
Transfer the content of a single cuvette into a 15-ml Falcon tube containing 10 ml of ES cell medium with a 1-ml plastic pipette.
Rinse each cuvette twice with 1 ml of ES cell medium to recover additional cells.
Plate 2 ml aliquots of each experimental cuvette (1:5 ratio) into three 10-cm dishes.
Plate two dishes (2 ml each) for the pDIRE cuvette.
Place the plates into the tissue culture incubator.
After at least 24 hours, exchange the medium for fresh ES cell medium without selective drug to allow recovery of the electroporated ES cells.
Gently change the medium after 24 hours to avoid detaching ES cells from gelatin.
Two days following electroporation, exchange the experimental dishes' medium for ES medium supplemented with appropriate selective drug.
Provide one control dish with regular ES cell medium and another with medium containing the selective drug.
Label the control plate without selective drug as a positive growth control clearly.
Change the selection and control medium daily.
Wash the plate three times with D-PBS once ES cells in the control dish become sub-confluent.
Extract genomic DNA from washed plates (see part 8).
Validate PCR primer pairs designed to detect wild-type, conditional and deleted alleles prior to isolation of ES cell colonies.
Spot ES cell colonies by the naked eye through the bottom of the tissue culture dish.
Circle identified ES cell colonies using a marker.
Screen circled colonies under the microscope for ES cells with round, defined borders.
Add 40 μl of cold Trypsin-EDTA (1x) per well into two rows of a 96 multi-well plate (24 wells in total; with U-shaped bottom).
Keep the plate on ice.
Replace the medium in the dish with 8 ml of D-PBS (with Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺).
Pick an isolated ES cell colony using a Gilson P20 pipette set to 10 μl.
Transfer the picked ES cell colony into a well of the 96-well plate on ice.
Incubate cells in the trypsin solution for 7 minutes at 37°C.
Replace the D-PBS in the plate with fresh medium containing the selective drug and return it to the tissue culture incubator.
After Trypsin digestion, add 175 μl of ES cell medium without selection to each well using a multi-dispenser pipette.
Gently disperse cells by pipetting up and down a few times with a Gilson P200 pipette set at 170 μl.
Transfer the single cell suspension to one well of a 48 multi-well plate containing Mitomycin C-treated feeder cells in 300 μl of ES cell medium without selective drug.
Return the 48 multi-well plate to the incubator.
Inspect the ES cell colonies under the microscope for viability and density.
Exchange the medium by adding 500 μl of fresh ES cell medium.
Flame the tip of the pipette after each aspiration to avoid cross-contamination between wells.
Add new medium to the side of the wells using a multi-dispenser pipette.
Avoid touching the borders of the wells when adding new medium.
Aspirate the ES cell medium from the wells.
Wash the wells with 75 μl of Trypsin-EDTA (1x).
Exchange the 75 μl Trypsin-EDTA (1x, 75 μl) solution once.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 8-10 minutes.
Remove media from a new 48 multi-well plate with Mitomycin C-treated feeder cells.
Replenish the well with 300 μl of ES cell medium.
Tap the plate containing the ES cell colonies gently.
Pipette up and down three times using a Gilson P200 pipette set at 60 μl.
Add 600 μl of ES cell medium to inactivate the Trypsin.
Pipette up and down four times using a Gilson P1000 pipette set to 500 μl.
Transfer 200 μl of ES cell suspension into a single well of the new 48 multi-well plate.
Return the plate with transferred cells to the incubator.
Transfer remaining ES cell suspension to a 1.5ml Eppendorf tube for DNA extraction.
Monitor the cells under the microscope the following day.
Change the medium for further expansion.
Lysate the cell pellet using 400 μl of lysis buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0; 50 mM EDTA; 100 mM NaCl; 0.5% SDS) supplemented with 1 mg/ml of Proteinase K.
Incubate for 2 hours at 55°C.
Spin briefly to concentrate the liquid at the bottom of the 1.5-ml tube.
Add 350 μl of digestion buffer (without Proteinase K) and 250 μl of 6M NaCl.
Mix by inverting the tube several times.
Centrifuge the tubes for 10 minutes at 13,000 rpm in a microcentrifuge.
Transfer the supernatant (contains genomic DNA) to a new 1.5-ml tube containing 500 μl of isopropanol.
Mix by gentle inversion for two minutes and re-centrifuge for 10 minutes at 13,000 rpm.
Carefully decant the supernatant.
Add 1 ml of 70% ethanol and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 13,000 rpm.
Remove the supernatant by careful decanting and ensure that the DNA pellet is not lost.
Re-centrifuge the tubes and remove any residual ethanol using a thin tip.
Air-dry the DNA pellets for 15 minutes.
Resuspend the DNA pellets in 50-100 μl of 10 mM Tris-Cl, 100 μM EDTA (pH 8.0) depending on pellet size.
Leave the solution for several hours to overnight at 4°C to resuspend.
Mix by brief vortexing and use 1-3 μl of DNA solution per PCR reaction in a total volume of 50 μl.
Mark the correctly replaced clones in the 48 multi-well plates.
Select ES cell clones with good colony morphology and ready to be split 48 hours after plating.
Trypsinize selected ES cell clones.
Transfer cells into one well of a 24 multi-well plate containing Mitomycin C-treated feeders in ES cell medium.
Remove additional positive clones from the 48 multi-well plate.
Gently add 400 μl of ice-cold freezing media to removed clones.
Seal the plate with Parafilm and wrap it in a plastic bag.
Transfer the sealed plate to -80°C into a Styrofoam box for storage.
Change ES cell medium daily.
Split cells every 2 days from a single 24-well to a single 6 well, then into a 10-cm tissue culture dish containing Mitomycin C treated feeder cells.
Take 1/5 of the single cell suspension when ready to split into a 10-cm dish.
Plate it into one gelatin-coated well of a 6 multi-well plate for karyotyping.
Label 5 cryotubes per 10-cm dish of ES cells for long-term storage.
Check the 10-cm dishes of ES cells for optimal confluency (70%) and colony morphology.
Change the media 2-3 hours before initiating the freezing process.
Trypsinize the ES cells as described.
Centrifuge the trypsinized ES cells.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 ml of ice-cold freezing medium in a 15-ml tube on ice.
Add an additional 3 ml of freezing media to the tube.
Aliquot the 5 ml of cell suspension into the 5 cryotubes (1 ml each).
Transfer the tubes to a Styrofoam holder.
Wrap the Styrofoam holder with bubble-wrap.
Place the wrapped package at -80°C.
The next day, transfer cryotubes individually into a cell freezing box that fits into liquid nitrogen tank for long-term storage.
